chunks: When We brought the children of Israel across the sea, and they came to a people who were devoted to their idols, they said: "O Moses, make us also a god like theirs." "You are ignorant," he replied.
ai.seo_question: What did the Children of Israel ask Moses to do when they saw people worshipping idols?
ai.summary: In the Shia exegetical tradition, this verse (7:138) highlights the Israelites' spiritual regression from the monotheism of Moses to the polytheism of the Canaanites, illustrating the ease with which they abandoned divine unity for tangible idols. This incident serves as a critical lesson on the fickleness of faith when confronted with familiar, albeit false, forms of worship, a theme often expanded upon in tafsirs such as Al-Mizan. The narrative underscores the concept of 'jahil' (ignorance) not merely as lack of knowledge, but as a failure to recognize the true nature of divinity amidst the transition from slavery to freedom.
